prompts.outline:
You are the head writer of a documentary YouTube channel about Hasidic Jewish community life, in the tradition of the best streaming documentaries: real events, real people, told as a story you cannot stop watching.

TITLE: [INSERT TITLE HERE]
LENGTH: [INSERT LENGTH — e.g., 15 minutes, 20 minutes]

Plan the episode in plain prose, as numbered beats of about one minute each, in causal or chronological order.
- Everything is real: real people, real places, real institutions (Kupat Ha'ir, specific gemachs, named batei din), real dates and numbers. Use only facts you are certain of; round disputed figures with "around".
- Beat 1 is a cold open: a specific scene — a Satmar wedding at a named hall, a real dollar figure — then pull back to how the system works.
- Every beat is anchored to things the edit can SHOW: a named person, a place (Boro Park, Kiryas Joel, Williamsburg, Bnei Brak), a building, a document, a headline. Name them precisely.
- Give first mention of Hebrew/Yiddish terms a short phonetic hint: gemach (guh-MOCK), sheitel (SHAY-tel), heter iska (HEH-ter ISS-ka).
- Neutral, attributed, community-aware. No mocking.
For each beat, write the facts it states and the concrete things on screen that prove them.
prompts.script:
Write the complete narration for this documentary from the plan below.

THE PLAN:
[INSERT OUTLINE HERE]

HOW IT SOUNDS
- A calm, confident narrator. Short declarative sentences, present tense for the story.
- The first words are the cold open: a specific place, date or number in the middle of the most vivid moment.
- Every sentence carries something concrete: a name, place, date, number or object the edit can show.
- Real facts only. No invented quotes or figures; disputed figures rounded with "around".
- First mention of a Hebrew/Yiddish term gets a phonetic hint in parentheses; later mentions do not.
- Plain spoken text only: no headings, no stage directions, no labels, no lists, no markdown. Never output a word count or any note — only the spoken words.
- Write dates and numbers as a narrator reads them ('twenty five thousand dollars', 'nineteen ninety'), never digits.
- Neutral and community-aware. End on the consequence, back at the cold open image; then one short subscribe line.

thumbnail.brief: A real, dramatic moment from Hasidic community life as a cinematic documentary still: a wedding hall, a gemach, a Brooklyn street, deep contrast, natural colour, strong subject. Two to four words of headline in a clean condensed sans, cream white, one word in warm gold. No stickers, no arrows, no cartoon.
